Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:12:1.hebrew: הרחיבה - אחד חופר בור י', ובא חבירו והרחיב פיו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:12:1.english: He widened it - One [person] digs a pit of ten [handbreadths], and another comes and widens its mouth.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:12:2.english: Behold, he has reduced the fumes - And may a blessing come upon him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:12:3.hebrew: הרי קירב הזיקא - שמיעט מקום מעמד רגלים, ושמא לא היה הולך השור עד מקום פי הבור שבתחילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:12:3.english: Behold, he has brought the damage closer - For he has reduced the space for [an animal's] feet to stand, and perhaps the ox would not have walked as far as the place of the original mouth of the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:15:1.hebrew: וראשון מאימת מיפטר - דניטעון על השני היתה השמירה? דפשיטא לן דהני עבר דקתני מתני', נשתמש קאמר; דאי כדקתני מתני' שעברו עליו שניהן זה אחר זה, אמאי ראשון פטור? הרי גם הוא פשע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:15:1.english: And from what point is the first exempt - That we should claim, "The guarding [of the pit] was upon the second"? For it is obvious to us that this "passed by" that the Mishnah teaches means "used [it]"; for if [it were literally] as the Mishnah teaches, that both of them passed by it one after the other, why is the first exempt? Behold, he too was negligent!

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:15:2.hebrew: דליו - כסוי הבור לכסותו, שהראשון פתחו ודלה, ובא שני ומצאו, ומסר לו ראשון את כיסוי הבור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:15:2.english: His bucket - [That is,] the cover of the pit, to cover it; for the first [partner] opened it and drew [water], and the second came and found it [open], and the first handed over to him the cover of the pit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:18:1.hebrew: והאי מדידיה קממלא - ולא הוי ליה שני שואל על חלקו של ראשון, שיהא כולו מוטל עליו לשומרו. הלכך, אם הזיק, שניהם חייבין. אבל מסר לו את הדלי, נעשה זה שומר שקיבל עליו לכסותו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:18:1.english: And this one is filling from his own - and the second [partner] is not [considered] a borrower with respect to the first [partner]'s share, such that all of it would be incumbent upon him to guard. Therefore, if [the cistern] caused damage, both of them are liable. However, [if] he handed the bucket over to him, this one becomes a guardian who has accepted upon himself to cover it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:19:1.english: To the courtyard - [Belonging to] both of them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:19:2.hebrew: לתוך שלו - כל היכא דעייל, יכול לומר: זה חלקי שאני בורר, ומהני ליה ברירה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:19:2.english: Into his [own] - Wherever he enters, he can say, "This is my portion that I am designating," and retroactive designation is effective for him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:1:1.hebrew: לימא הא - דקתני חייבין, רבי היא, דאמר לעיל גבי חופר בור תשעה, הואיל ועבד בו שיעור נזקין, דהוי שותף בנזקין. והכא, דעבדי קמאי שיעור מיתה, הוו כולם שותפין בתשלומי מיתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:1:1.english: Shall we say [that] this - which teaches [that they are] liable, is [the view of] Rabbi, who said earlier regarding one who digs a pit [of] nine [handbreadths] [that] since he made in it the measure [sufficient] for damages, he is a partner in the damages. And here, where the first ones made the measure [sufficient] for death, they are all partners in the payment for death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:1:2.english: And this [baraita] - which teaches [that] the last one is liable and the first one is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:1:3.english: The Rabbis - who infer [from the phrase "a man"] one [person], and not two.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:21:1.hebrew: ליקנייה בחזקה - משנשתמש בו, שהרי קרקע נקנית בכסף, בשטר ובחזקה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:21:1.english: Let him acquire it by taking possession - Once he uses it, since land is acquired by money, by a deed, and by taking possession.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:22:1.hebrew: לעולם בחזקה - לבד מסירת דליו בעי לאחזוקי ביה, ומיהו להכי מהני מסירה, דאי בחזקה לחודה, בעי למימר ליה "לך חזק וקני" כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:22:1.english: Actually, [it is] through taking possession - Besides the handing over of his bucket, he must take possession of it; however, the handing over is effective for this [purpose], for if [it were] through taking possession alone, he would have to say to him, "Go, take possession, and acquire," etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:2:1.hebrew: אפילו רבנן מודו - דכי כתיב מיעוטא, אחופר בור ט' כתיב, דליכא לחיוביה מן "והמת יהיה לו"; דהא מסקנא דמילתא מן "והמת יהיה לו" נפקא לן, דההוא דעבד שיעור מיתה מחייב. ומיהו כולה מילתא לא מצינו למילף מינה, דעיקר קרא לכדרבא אתא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:2:1.english: Even the Rabbis concede - For when the exclusionary [clause] is written, it is written regarding one who digs a pit of nine [handbreadths], so that one cannot hold him liable from [the verse] "and the dead [animal] shall be his"; for the conclusion of the matter is derived from "and the dead [animal] shall be his" — that the one who made the measurement [sufficient for] death is liable. However, we could not derive the entire matter from it [alone], because the primary [purpose of] the verse comes for Rava's [teaching].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:2:2.english: The Rabbis - Who infer: one man, and not two.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:3:1.hebrew: שלא היה בה הבל למיתה - שהיתה רחבה הרבה. מש"ה פטור אף בנזקין, כדאמרינן: "איש אחד" ולא שנים, דהוה ליה כחופר בור ט' ובא אחר והשלימה לעשרה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:3:1.english: [Where] it did not have fumes [capable of leading] to death - Because it was very wide. Therefore, [the first person] is exempt even for injuries, as we say: "One man," and not two, for it is like one who digs a pit of nine [handbreadths] and another comes and completes it to ten.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:4:1.hebrew: הא והא רבי - דאילו רבנן, כי היכי דפטרי חופר ט' מנזקין, פטרי נמי הכא לקמאי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:4:1.english: This and that are [in accordance with] Rabbi - For whereas the Rabbis, just as they exempt one who digs nine [handbreadths] from [liability for] damages, they also exempt the earlier ones here.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:4:2.hebrew: כגון שלא היה בו הבל לא למיתה ולא לנזקין - הלכך, ראשון פטור אף בנזקין. ואליבא דרב, דאמר "להבלו ולא לחבטו", ואליבא דרבי, אצטריך לשנויי שלא היה בו הבל אפי' לנזקין, דאילו היה בו הבל לנזקין — הוי ראשון שותף לנזקין. ולשמואל, דאמר "אף על החבטה חייבה תורה", מוקי לה במלא ספוגות בקרקעותיו, דאין כאן חבט:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:4:2.english: Where it did not have fumes, neither for death nor for damages - Therefore, the first [person] is exempt even for damages. And according to Rav, who says [the Torah made one liable for a pit] "for its fumes and not for its impact," and according to Rabbi, it was necessary to answer that it did not have fumes even for damages; for if it had fumes for damages, the first [person] would be a partner in [liability for] the damages. And according to Shmuel, who says "the Torah also made [one] liable for the impact," he establishes it [as referring to a pit] filled with sponges at its bottom, where there is no impact.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:5:1.hebrew: באנו למחלוקת רבי ורבנן - לרבנן, אחרון חייב בין לנזקין בין למיתה; לרבי, אחר אחרון למיתה, אחר שניהן לנזקין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:5:1.english: We have arrived at the dispute [between] Rabbi and the Rabbis - According to the Rabbis, the last one is liable both for injuries and for death; according to Rabbi, [liability follows] the last one for death, [and] both of them for injuries.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:6:1.hebrew: פשיטא - מה לי הוסיף למטה, מה לי הוסיף למעלה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:6:1.english: [Isn't it] obvious - What difference does it make whether he added [to the pit] at the bottom or added at the top?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:6:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא - בין לרבי בין לרבנן, אחרון פטור, דלאו הבלא דידיה קטליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:6:2.english: Lest you say - Both according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and according to the Rabbis, the last one is exempt, because it is not his fumes that killed it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:7:1.hebrew: טם טפח - החופר בור ט', ואחר השלימו לעשרה, וחזר אחרון וסתם ומילא עפר אותו טפח שהוסיף:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:7:1.english: Closed up a handbreadth - One who digs a pit [of] nine [handbreadths], and another completed it to ten [handbreadths], and the latter went back and closed [it] up and filled with earth that handbreadth that he had added.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:7:2.hebrew: טם - סתם בלשון ארמי, [סתמום] טמונין פלשתאי (בראשית כו):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:7:2.english: Closed up [tam] - [This means] "stopped up" in Aramaic, [as in the Targum of] "[the Philistines] stopped them up" — temunin Pelishta'ei (Genesis 26[:15]).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:7:3.english: What he did, he removed - And the first [digger] is liable for damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:8:1.hebrew: קמה ליה ברשותיה - והוה ליה השתא בור תשעה דאחרון, וחייב מיהא בנזקין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 51b:8:1.english: It stands in his possession - and it is now a pit of nine [handbreadths] belonging to the latter [digger], and he is at least liable for damages.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 51b:13:1.hebrew: אי בהבלא מיית - הרבה הוא תימה, דנהי דמיעט הבלא, מכל מקום אם לא דהרחיב לא היה נופל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 51b:13:1.english: If [the animal] died because of the [lethal] fumes - This is very astonishing, for granted that he reduced the [lethal] fumes, nevertheless, had he not widened [the pit], it would not have fallen [in].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 51b:19:1.hebrew: השותפין שנדרו הנאה זה מזה אסורים ליכנס בחצר - בנדרים (דף מו:) מפרש: בין יש בה דין חלוקה ובין אין בה דין חלוקה אסורים; ואע"פ שאין יכול למחות ליכנס כשאין בו דין חלוקה, מ"מ יכול לאסור עליו, מידי דהוי אמשכיר בית לחבירו שיכול המשכיר להקדיש — כדאיתא במסכת ערכין בפ' האומר משקלי (דף כא. ושם) — אע"פ שאין יכול למחות ביד השוכר שלא ליכנס. וא"ת: ומ"ש מב"ח דאתי ושקיל אפי' הקדיש שדהו, אלא משום דר' אבהו "מוסיף דינר שלא יאמר כו'" (שם דף כג:)? וי"ל: דשאני ב"ח, דגוף הקרקע יוצא מתחת יד המקדיש; אבל גבי שוכר, לעולם אין גוף הקרקע יוצא מתחת יד המשכיר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 51b:19:1.english: Partners who vowed [not to derive] benefit from each other are prohibited from entering the courtyard - In Nedarim (46b) [the Gemara] explains: whether it has the law of division or does not have the law of division, they are prohibited; and even though [one] cannot object to [the other] entering when it does not have the law of division, nevertheless he can prohibit [it] upon him, just as in the case of one who rents out a house to his fellow, where the landlord can consecrate [it] — as it is stated in Tractate Arakhin in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer Mishkali (21a, and there) — even though he cannot object to the tenant's entering. And if you will ask: How is this different from a creditor, who comes and takes [the field] even if [the debtor] consecrated his field, except because of Rabbi Abbahu['s enactment that] "he adds a dinar so that [people] will not say, etc." (there, 23b)? And one can answer: A creditor is different, because the essence of the land leaves the possession of the consecrator; whereas with a tenant, the essence of the land never leaves the possession of the landlord.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 51b:3:1.english: Where it did not have fumes [capable of causing] death - Because its width was greater than its depth.
